---

I am an assistant professor (with tenure) in the Department of Political Science at Trinity College Dublin. I received my Ph.D. from Columbia University in 2016 and was previously a postdoctoral associate at NYU Abu Dhabi.

My research focuses on authoritarian politics in Putin-era Russia: how autocratic regimes sustain themselves, how the mass public understands their authoritarian environment, and why corruption persists. I use quantitative methods and original micro-level data, including the largest individual-level database of Russian public opinion survey responses.

My work has appeared in the *American Political Science Review*, *American Journal of Political Science*, *Comparative Political Studies*, *Comparative Politics*, *Journal of Experimental Political Science*, *Europe-Asia Studies*, and *Post-Soviet Affairs*.

*(Looking for Noah M. Buckley-Farlee? That's me.)*

## Research interests

Comparative politics · authoritarian politics · Russian and post-communist politics · public opinion · corruption · political methodology · bureaucracy · policing
